summary.intent: Land a stacked pair of oracle branches (function-marker-rule and tool-adapters) produced by a background worker for trail 153, by verifying signatures, pushing, and linking them.
summary.outcome: The worker finished both branches with passing checks; the assistant verified both commits were signed and pushed the first branch (function-marker-rule). The second branch push, PRs and the three-tools-report branch remain.

repo: Oracle branches are stacked: oracle/function-marker-rule is based on main, and oracle/tool-adapters is based on oracle/function-marker-rule, so the base must be linked with --base before any PR exists.
The oracle suite is run with oxfmt --check, oxlint and typos; the Rust suite and TS package tests are skipped when only apps/oracle and scripts change.
Under the sandbox, tsx fails on its IPC socket (EPERM); running `node src/oracle.ts ...` works because Node 26 strips types.
react-docgen follows imports via its default fsImporter, so the docs claim that it reads each file alone was wrong; it still throws on 17-21% of files (antd 51/295, shadcn 265/1240).
scripts/weekly.py counts @types/react props, so the RDT dump must not filter to own props; scripts/rdt.mjs keeps `type` and adds `typeObject` for non-@types/react props.
scripts/weekly.py line 7 repeats the outdated 'reads each file alone' wording and belongs to another worker.
Unreadable type text maps to opaque in the adapters, which scores 'less precise' and never 'wrong'.
The function-marker rule change leaves Caliper's antd and shadcn oracle reports identical because Caliper records neither optional nor rest markers.

code.finding: Function-type cap rule is now (kp.optional && !cp.optional) || (kp.rest && !cp.rest), capping only a parameter marker the tool lost.
New file with a single TS-text mapper typeFromText plus rdtNorm and rdgNorm adapters, tested by 13 tests built from real Segmented output.
Passage reworded to fix the incorrect claim that react-docgen reads files alone.

workflow: Verify commit signatures on worker-produced branches before pushing.
Background worktree agents leave work committed locally and unpushed, so the parent must push and link the branches.
Land the pairing branches before oracle/three-tools-report, which depends on them.

friction: tsx IPC socket EPERM under the sandbox forced use of plain node for running the oracle.
react-docgen throws on 17-21% of files, reducing coverage.
No spectrum corpus is installed locally, which blocked investigating its 1.09% oracle wrong-rate.
The numbers came from an Oct-30 binary in another worktree rather than a fresh build of main.
open_items: Push oracle/tool-adapters and open PRs for both branches, with tool-adapters based on function-marker-rule.
Build oracle/three-tools-report: match the RDT and react-docgen dumps to checker exports by (rel(file), normComponent(name)) and wire rdt_out and rdg_out through scripts/weekly.py.
Investigate Spectrum's 1.09% oracle wrong-rate by running the weekly workflow on a branch with the oracle's --dump flag.
Validate the function-marker rule and adapters on Mantine, Chakra and Spectrum via a CI weekly run.
Fix the outdated 'reads each file alone' wording at scripts/weekly.py line 7, owned by another worker.
The Rust suite and TS package tests were not run, since no Rust or packages/ code changed.
